segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين
[unclear] of Surah Yusuf. After Benjamin remained in Egypt, and after his brothers had tried everything to get him released, and when they had lost all hope, they withdrew

to consult one another: what should they do now? And the eldest of their brothers says to them: "You know well," he says, "that you gave a promise to our father, you swore that you would bring Benjamin back.
You swore that you would bring Benjamin back, and before that you went too far with regard to Yusuf."

That is, you threw him into the well, or you wanted to kill him. And, Allah knows best, this is the brother who took pity when they wanted to kill him, and said: "Do not kill Yusuf, but throw him into the well."

After this brother, the eldest, convinced them that he would not return to Palestine until his father permitted him, or until Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, decided, he advised them how to justify themselves before their father.
In what way? He says to them: "Irji'u ila abikum" – he says: go back to your father, to Yaqub – "fa qulu ya abana innabnaka saraqa" – and say: "Father, our father, your son Benjamin has stolen.
He has stolen." And they say: "We bear witness only to what we saw, to what we saw with our own eyes, when that inspector, or Yusuf, pulled that vessel out of his load."

And they say: "We did not know that this would happen; we do not know the ghayb (the unseen), we do not know what will happen; only Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, knows the unseen. We do not know; had we known the unseen, we would not have taken our brother Benjamin with us, we would not have brought him along. But what happened happened."
What does Yaqub, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him), say to them? He says: "What you have done, my sons," he says, "it is only your souls that made this deed," he says, "seem fair to you."
Just as your soul, your nafs, made that deed seem fair to you, that is, the evil that you did to Yusuf, so now you have repeated, repeated the same deed.

"So," he says, "patience is beautiful" – with beautiful patience (sabr), which is accompanied neither by lamenting nor by complaint. He goes on, he says: "I ask Allah and I hope that Yusuf, and Benjamin, and this eldest son of mine will return to me. Truly," he says, "He knows well what state I am in, what my grief is." Al-Hakim – He is Wise and knows why it is,

why it is like this, why all this is happening to me. So Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, out of His wisdom, knows why certain things happen to His servants. It goes on: so he, alayhis-salatu was-salam, turned away from them, from his sons, and said: "O Yusuf, my sorrow!" This reminded him of what these brothers had done to Yusuf 30 years earlier, it reminded him of it and renewed his pain. And truly, dear brothers,

time cannot heal a certain pain. Time can only cover the pain, but it can never heal it. So whenever a person goes through some situation that reminds him of the pain he already had, it only renews it for him, as if it had just begun. So when a loved one passes away, a mother, a father and so on, time only masks it, but when something reminds him of his father, his mother and so on, or of a brother who passed away, it all immediately comes back to him,
as if he had passed away today. So, it says, Yaqub's eyes turned white from sorrow, from pain. "Fa huwa kazim" – it says: he was full of pain.
He was in pain. What do these sons of his say, looking at him like this? They say: "He still…" – they are astonished, they say: "He still," they say, "mentions Yusuf."

He has not forgotten him. That after 30 years he has not forgotten him! They say: "Hatta takuna haradan aw takuna minal-halikin" – they say: "Either he will fall gravely ill, or he will," they say, "die. There is nothing else for him."

What does he say? What does Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, say: "Innama ashku bathi wa huzni ilallah" – he says: "Truly, I lay my grief and my pain before Allah," subhanallah. See how Yaqub, alayhis-salam, did not want to complain to anyone except Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And this is how a believer should complain and lay his pain, his sorrow, before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Because, believe me, it happens that a person lays out his pain, his sorrow, before his wife –

she will immediately say: "Weakling," she will, wallahi, she will immediately say: "Look at him, a weakling." You fall in her eyes. In front of your friends it's the same, they say: "Look at him," they say, "a weakling, he's good for nothing, he's not strong." And then a person falls in the eyes of others, whereas Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is surely the One who will listen to our complaint.
And, in sha Allah, [unclear] to His servant, He will not send him away empty-handed. Yaqub, alayhis-salam, says: "And I know from Allah what you do not know."
I know what you do not know. Why? Because Yaqub, knowing the dream that Yusuf had seen, Yaqub, alayhis-salam, knew that Yusuf was alive, and that in the end the dream Yusuf had seen would come true.

But, dear brothers, [unclear] we must understand Yaqub's pain. Why? Yaqub knew that Yusuf was alive, but it still hurt him. It hurts a parent: he does not know where his child is, in what condition. We send our children off, or someone sends a child abroad, he knows that the child has a flat, that he has a good job and all that,

and despite that a person worries about that child. Let alone Yaqub, who did not know where Yusuf was, in slavery, what his condition was and so on. But he knew from Allah what his brothers, that is, his sons, did not know. He knew that Yusuf was alive, and that, in sha Allah, the dream Yusuf had seen would come true.

"Ya baniyyadh-habu fa tahassasu min Yusufa wa akhihi" – he says: "O my sons, go," he says, "[unclear], and inquire about Yusuf and his brother Benjamin." "Wa la tay'asu min rawhillah" – and he says: "do not," he says, "lose hope in Allah's mercy." "Innahu la yay'asu min rawhillahi illal-qawmul-kafirun" – he says: only the unbelievers lose hope in Allah's mercy, only the unbelievers lose hope in Allah's mercy.

And this reminds me of the verse, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Ya 'ibadiyal-ladhina asrafu 'ala anfusihim" – O My servants, who have lost, that is, who have transgressed against themselves, who have gone to excess in sinning – "la taqnatu min rahmatillah" – He says: do not lose hope in Allah's mercy.

Truly Allah, He says, forgives all sins. So even if a person's sins were like the heavens and the Earth, and after that he repented sincerely, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, Allah would forgive him. It often happens to a person that, let's say, he sins, and thinks that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will not forgive him.

And it happens to me quite often that someone comes to me and says: "Effendi, I have committed this and this and this sin. And I have lost hope. I don't know whether Allah will forgive me," and yet he has repented. And believe me, this drives quite a few people to abandon everything, the prayer and all. He has lost hope in Allah's mercy. He has committed so many sins that he has lost hope in Allah's mercy.

Allah forgives the sins of whoever sincerely, sincerely repents, however great those sins may be. Yaqub, alayhis-salam, ordered them to return to Egypt and to search for Yusuf and his brother Benjamin. That is enough for today, in sha Allah, and tomorrow we continue. There is not much left, just a little more is left. May Allah reward you with every good.
